Loans / EXPLAINER

Questions to ask before taking out a loan

Compare the total cost and repayment terms before relying on a monthly payment alone.

FH
FinancersHub editorial team
Editorial preview · Educational guide

Original editorial image for the FinancersHub design preview.

A manageable payment can hide an expensive loan if the term is long or fees are high. Compare offers using the same borrowing amount and repayment assumptions.

KEEP IN MIND

Three questions to ask

  1. 01What are the APR, fees, and total payments?
  2. 02Can the rate or payment change?
  3. 03What happens if you pay early or late?

Look at more than the payment

Ask for the annual percentage rate, total repayment amount, term, and any origination or other fees. APR incorporates certain borrowing costs beyond the interest rate, but the dollars paid over the full loan also matter.

Test the schedule against your budget

Find out when payments begin, whether the rate can change, and what happens if you miss a payment. A longer term can reduce a monthly payment while increasing the overall cost. Check the final disclosure before accepting.

Compare the same kind of offer

Use the same loan amount and term when possible, and ask each lender to explain unfamiliar charges. If an offer has a feature you value, weigh it against its total cost rather than assuming the lowest advertised rate is automatically best.

SOURCE & FURTHER READING

Check the primary source

The guide is newly written for this preview and draws its factual background from Consumer Financial Protection Bureau: Loan interest rate and APR ↗. Check that source and current product terms before making a decision.
